Class ClientSprint

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.env.ClientSprint
public final class ClientSprint extends Object
Sprinting as a real game client keeps it, and what the server gets to hear of it. A body that has no client of its own (a fake player) is run through this so that its sprint hits come out exactly as they would if the same keys were pressed on a real client.

The rules are the game's (1.21.11, LocalPlayer.aiStep and Player.attack):

  • Sprinting starts with W held and the sprint key, or with W tapped twice within seven ticks. It lasts until W is let go or the player runs into something.
  • A hit made while sprinting with the weapon charged knocks back, and stops the sprint: on the server, and on the client. The client starts sprinting again in the same tick if the sprint key is still held.
  • The server is only told when the client's sprint has changed by the end of a tick. A sprint that was stopped by a hit and restarted in the same tick has not changed, so the server goes on believing the sprint is over and the next hits do not knock back, until the sprint really stops for a tick (W or the sprint key let go) and starts again.
  • A click is sent before the tick's movement, so a hit is judged with the sprint the server knew of before this tick's keys.
